quotes.name: Mark Aitken
quotes.quote: One year says I'm not done yet, and it says I didn't want to pretend I knew what next winter looks like. The money being the same as last year — that was never the point. I've got three kids who know this city as home, and a program in East Oakland that's about to start its sixth summer. Colorado gave me a place to play at the level I expect from myself, and I'm going to give them everything I've got for 2042. But I'm not going to stand here and tell you I've closed the book on Oakland. That door doesn't lock from my side. It just doesn't.

The free agency question this page has carried since C112 has its answer, and it is not Oakland and it is not Anaheim. Mark Aitken has signed with the Colorado Rockies, one year for $21 million. The Angels were the team with the reported interest in C116, the A's were the team with the history, and Colorado is the team that closed. The money is almost exactly what he made in 2041, $21. 4M, so this was never about Aitken being priced as a player in decline.
Current cycle: C117

He is coming off a . 283 season with 153 hits, 33 homeruns, 87 RBI and 3. 2 WAR in 540 at bats, a 93 overall first baseman with 3 Gold Gloves and the 2037 Playoff MVP, and he homered in the World Series that clinched the seventh title. The length is the detail that will be argued over. One year is a short commitment for a player at the top of the market, and it puts Aitken back in free agency after 2042.

Whether that reads as a door left open or simply the deal that was there, he has not said. What it leaves behind in Oakland is bigger than a lineup spot. Aitken is an Oakland native who grew up swinging a bat in East Oakland. He owns his place in Jack London, where he lives with his wife and three kids. He has been the A's player rep and community liaison, and he runs Aitken Little Leaguers, free baseball for East Oakland kids heading into its sixth year.
Mark Aitken — First Baseman, Colorado Rockies
